deities: Goddess Kankali Mata (a form of Goddess Kali)

history.summary: Shakti shrine dedicated to Kankali Mata (Kali) in the Laxmisagar locality near the Rambagh Fort complex, about 2 km from Darbhanga Junction. The goddess is described in local accounts as the kuldevi (family deity) of the Darbhanga royal family; worship was traditionally conducted under their patronage and the temple later opened to the public. It is noted for tantric forms of worship historically prevalent in Mithila. NOTE: detailed foundation records are absent from published sources - one local review credits Maharajadhiraj Kameshwar Singh with building it and a YouTube documentary calls it nearly 250 years old; both are unverified. Coordinates are street-level approximations (Laxmisagar area).

name: Kankali Temple, Darbhanga
town_description: Darbhanga is a major city in north Bihar's Mithila region and the former seat of the Darbhanga Raj, whose palaces, forts, temples and ponds (such as Harahi and Dighi) dot the city. It hosts Lalit Narain Mithila University and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University, and its many Kali and Durga temples - including the famous Shyama Mai temple - make it a noted centre of Shakti worship.

travel.railway: Darbhanga Junction, about 2 km from the temple (per Wikipedia)
travel.road: Laxmisagar locality, Darbhanga city; reachable by auto-rickshaw and city bus

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant weather; general Mithila guidance, not temple-published)
